To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) reliable long period response spectral ordinate information can be obtained from digital accelerograms by double integration of their acceleration waveforms without the need to remove the baseline drift, and that (ii) a noise index can be used to quantify the difference between the response spectral ordinates obtained from the original acceleration record and the spurious acceleration record obtained from the original record contaminated by random long term noise.
1. The displacement waveform of a digital SM record is not necessarily free of spurious baseline drift to yield unreliable long period response spectral ordinate.

the displacement wave from the double integration of the acceleration record does not need to be free of baseline drift to provide reliable spectral ordinates for periods up to about 10 s, and that the noise index, which can be calculated based on the acceleration and velocity waveform, provides a useful criterion for the selection of reliable digital records for the estimation of long period response spectra.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following two aspects: First, we investigate whether reliable long period response spectra can be obtained by double integration and spectral analysis of accelerograms obtained from strong-motion instruments.

the following issues: (1) the reliability of displacement waveforms obtained from digital accelerograms by double integration; (2) the effect on the reliability of long-period response spectral ordinates of the baseline drifts in the displacement waveform; (3) the development of a simple and effective method of identifying and removing baseline drifts in displacement waveforms; and (4) the development of an objective method for evaluating the reliability of longperiod response spectral ordinates.

the following issues: 1. the use of digital strong motion records in the frequency domain to determine long period response spectra; 2. the effect of baseline drift on the displacement waveform and the long period response spectral ordinate; 3. the effect of long period random noise on the displacement waveform, the velocity and the long period spectral ordinate; and 4. a method for selecting digital records for use in long period response spectral analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the long period response spectra from the broadband records are generally more reliable than those from the digital SM records, but the latter can also yield reliable results, especially when the noise index is low.

the long period response spectrum of a digital accelerogram is reliable if the displacement waveform obtained by double integration is free of unrealistic baseline shifts, which is a condition that can be checked by visual inspection.

the use of digital accelerograms for the determination of long period response spectra is feasible and reliable, but the reliability depends upon the quality of the data, the selection of appropriate filtering, and, of course, the quality of the analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can use the digital records for long period response spectrum estimation without filtering them, and the noise index can be used to quantify the reliability of the digital records.

, for the purposes of estimating long period ground motion response, the use of digital strong motion records is justified, provided the records have a sufficiently long duration to include the long period content.
we have developed objective criteria for the selection of reliable digital strong motion records for use in ground motion predictions at periods longer than 2 s.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the purpose of long period spectral ordinatess, the displacement response spectrum can be obtained by simply double integrating the accelerogram.

, if we have a digital strong motion record that we want to use for ground motion prediction at long period, we can first look at the velocity waveform and if we see that the velocity waveform has some long period noise, we can then calculate a noise index.
, for ground motion prediction at long periods, one can use the raw accelerograms without any filtering or baseline correction.
